question.text: A call option is said to be in-the-money (ITM) when:

answer.text: The underlying price is greater than the strike price
The underlying price is less than the strike price
The underlying price equals the strike price
The option premium is greater than the strike price

explanation.text: The Logic: A call option is ITM when the underlying price is higher than the strike price, because the holder can buy at the strike and immediately sell at the higher market price for a positive intrinsic value. The Trap: Underlying lower than strike is OTM for calls (it is the ITM condition for puts), and underlying equal to strike is ATM. Comparing premium to strike is irrelevant to moneyness, which is defined by the underlying price versus the strike. Note: Rewrote the trap using words rather than raw comparison signs that can be swallowed in rendering, and removed the cross-exam and pro-tip paragraphs.
